incoming.explanation: The confirmed Gurney entries in the same register and hand are the comparator set for Entry E.
Entry E as re-read is the record the finding interprets.
The reading is AI-assisted paleography awaiting professional confirmation.
The estimated baptism date may precede the parents' marriage.
The absence of a John in the second family means any son John must belong to the first — which is where Entry E puts him.
A prior Gurney household in the parish removes the residual oddity of a Gurney baptism at East Dereham, easing the Entry E reading's setting without bearing on the letterform argument.

outgoing.explanation: A baptism of John son of Francis at East Dereham is the strongest single link in the argument.

shortLabel: Entry E is probably John Gurney-1's baptism

sources.locator: Norfolk Record Office, PD 86/41, image 00715, Entry E, as re-read

statement: Entry E is probably the baptism of John Gurney-1, making him the eldest known child of Francis Gurney by Margaret Rybett, born at East Dereham before the family moved to London. The reading is the strongest single link between the Massachusetts emigrant and the Norfolk Gurney line, and it is an inference from letterform comparison, not a legible entry.
